A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATOM/TG80 research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ATOM evaluations, ablations, computational measurements, and TG80 molecular-dynamics simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, connectivity and symmetry analyses, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: ATOM's equivariant lifting, heterogeneous attention, T-RoPE, noise regularization, positional encodings, and training objectives are retained. ATOM-GATv2 is introduced as a diagnostic comparison variant, without changing the proposed ATOM method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MD17, RMD17, MD22, and TG80 for the same molecular-trajectory prediction and generalization tasks. The added formic-acid comparison uses TG80; pooling its existing clusters changes the training protocol rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds MACE to MD17 accuracy comparisons in Table 1 and TG80 OOD comparisons in Table 3, and ATOM-GATv2 to MD22 in Table 2. New inference benchmarks compare against MACE-OFF24 and Lennard-Jones, plus AMBER on MD17, substantially broadening the comparator families.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct protocols for float32 inference timing at horizons 3000 and 10000 on MD17 and 3000 on MD22, pooled-TG80 versus single-task training under stated equal compute, and direct equivariance-defect evaluation. Existing accuracy protocols and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; these are additional evaluation designs.

E4.justification: New analyses test graph connectivity versus attention through ATOM-GATv2, quantify symmetry defects through Monte Carlo sampling, and compare joint versus single-task training for formic acid. Conversely, v1's explicit-hydrogen ablation and learned value-residual curves are removed, substantially revising the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 introduces Monte Carlo equivariance estimation using 20 random rotations and 10 timesteps, with 2SD intervals in Table 14. The general reporting of mean ±2σ over three training runs is retained; no increase in training-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing ATOM/EGNO accuracy entries are retained, but v2 adds baseline scores, symmetry estimates, rotation-penalty ratios, and inference timings. Table 13 reports single-task versus pooled-data formic-acid S2S errors of 26.40 versus 22.39, but S2T errors of 18.10 versus 18.72, all ×10^-2. Hydrogen-ablation results, residual curves, and the 20%-faster-training assertion are removed.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 newly formalizes ε-quasi-equivariance through a group-averaged transformation discrepancy, with a corresponding Monte Carlo estimator in Appendix E.3. The canonicalization derivations and Proposition G.1's kernel-integral proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about ATOM's design, TG80, single-task performance, and zero-shot generalization across molecules and time horizons. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies MACE comparisons because of different pretraining data and interprets the GATv2 control as evidence for fully connected interactions. It extends the proposed energy-based future direction to stochastic Langevin dynamics and removes the explicit-hydrogen failure explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds an ATOM/TG80 repository link, ASE and MACE-Torch versions, the MACE-OFF24 Medium checkpoint designation, and EGNO's previously missing 335770 parameter count. It also specifies fixed-horizon 3000 pretraining for the existing temporal-sweep analysis; this disclosure does not establish a rerun. Other dataset-release placeholders remain.

R1.justification: A new time-coarsened MD discussion substantially expands positioning among stochastic transition-kernel and deterministic large-stride methods, including Timewarp, Score Dynamics, UniSim, MDNet, and FlashMD. It frames ATOM as force-free, deterministic, parallel coarse-graining and adds an explicit comparison with EGNO.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local explanations are expanded, Appendix E is regrouped by experiment type, and conference and author text are updated. v2 also introduces unresolved RMD17 table references and an incorrect table reference for the equivariance estimates.

P2.justification: Tables 1–4 gain rows, four new appendix tables appear, and the old hydrogen table and residual-learning plot disappear. The pipeline graphic is updated, the TG80 construction diagram moves from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 9, and conference formatting and several captions change. These substantially alter the displays while retaining most existing plots.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons, connectivity control, symmetry diagnostics, and inference timings strengthen support for the existing claims. Removing the training-speed assertion inconsistent with the retained tables and adding a repository link also help. These gains are tempered by losing the explicit-hydrogen negative results and introducing broken table references, yielding a limited overall improvement.
